references.text: Moses describes similar fear and anguish that will strike Israel in exile—a trembling heart, wasted eyes, and a fainting soul, along with constant fear day and night.
The wicked flee though no one pursues, reflecting the same fear described in Leviticus where they flee without a pursuer.
Isaiah prophesies that a thousand will flee at the threat of one man, echoing the fear-driven flight in Leviticus.
Achan and Israel's sin led them to flee from their enemies, illustrating the fulfillment of the warning in Leviticus.
Job describes how the wicked hear terrifying sounds and dread destruction even in times of peace, similar to the terror described in Leviticus.
Describes how one will chase a thousand and two will put ten thousand to flight when the Lord has given them over, contrasting with those who flee without a pursuer.
